production.note: PROVISIONAL (a used-car report and databases). US model years. Consumer Guide's used-car report covers the '1995-99 Mitsubishi Eclipse' and says "the top-line GSX was equipped with all-wheel drive". KBB lists a 1995 'GSX Coupe 2D' (kbb-1995-eclipse-gsx) and a 1999 'GSX Coupe 2D' (kbb-1999-eclipse-gsx). The GS-T Spyder convertible (from 1996) is a separate, front-drive model.

body.note: KBB 'GSX Coupe 2D'; iSeeCars calls it a '2dr Hatchback' (liftback coupe, which the guide files as Coupe).

displacementL.note: 'Engine Size (liters/cubic inches): 2.0/122'. No opened page gave the cc figure.

aspiration.note: Consumer Guide: "A turbocharged 2.0-liter engine went into GS-T and GSX models, making 210 horsepower (205 horsepower when equipped with an automatic transmission)."

drivetrain.note: "The base RS, GS, and GS-T had front-wheel drive, while the top-line GSX was equipped with all-wheel drive." KBB: 'Drive Type AWD'.

transmission.note: "A 5-speed manual transmission was standard in all models, with 4-speed automatic optional." The turbo engine's table lists '5-speed manual 4-speed automatic'.

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL (database, with publications agreeing). Manual car. Quote (KBB 1995 Eclipse GSX Coupe 2D, whose page lists the transmission as Manual / 5 speed): "Horsepower 210 @ 6000 RPM". KBB 1999 GSX Coupe 2D: "210 @ 6000 RPM" (kbb-1999-eclipse-gsx). Consumer Guide (Tom Appel): "A turbocharged 2.0-liter engine went into GS-T and GSX models, making 210 horsepower (205 horsepower when equipped with an automatic transmission)." Adam Dixon's 1999 GSX review (reproduced by Curbside Classic): "210-horsepower, turbocharged 2.0-liter inline four" (curbside-1999-eclipse-gsx). The optional automatic is rated 205 hp.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (database). 1995 GSX coupe; KBB's 1995 GSX trim page lists the transmission as Manual / 5 speed (the manual is standard), so the figure is taken as the manual car's. Quote (KBB): "Curb Weight 3120 lbs." iSeeCars 1995 'AWD GSX Turbo 2dr Hatchback': 'Curb Weight | 3120 | lbs' (iseecars-1995-eclipse). Both databases also give the same 3,270 lb for 1999 (kbb-1999-eclipse-gsx, iseecars-1999-eclipse), so they share one data feed and count as one source. Reference year 1995, the launch year.

sources.title: 1995-99 Mitsubishi Eclipse (used car report, Tom Appel)

provisionalNote: Power (210 hp with the standard manual; 205 hp with the optional automatic) rests on KBB (1995 and 1999), with Consumer Guide (Tom Appel: 'making 210 horsepower (205 horsepower when equipped with an automatic transmission)') and a single 1999 review by Adam Dixon agreeing; weight (3,120 lb) rests on KBB and iSeeCars, which share one data feed (effectively one source); production years rest on Consumer Guide and KBB. A Mitsubishi Motors America press kit, brochure or spec sheet for the 1995 Eclipse GSX, or a major magazine specification panel, would replace them.
